name: Jellyscribe
overview: Real-time Letterboxd and Serializd diary sync with duplicate detection
description: Automatically syncs your Jellyfin watch history to your Letterboxd diary (films) and Serializd diary (TV). Supports multiple users, real-time sync on playback completion, duplicate detection, retry with backoff, and TMDb-based matching.

versions.changelog: The Jellyscribe pages are easier to read and use: history can be searched, TV episodes are grouped per show, older history can be loaded, errors show up instead of endless loading, account settings are grouped, and the page follows Jellyfin's dark theme on every device. Syncs are quicker and more reliable: scheduled syncs run at fixed times overnight, Serializd's slow wake-ups no longer fail a run, finished shows aren't rechecked every time, and the sync history stays small and can't be lost if Jellyfin stops mid-save. Jellyscribe no longer sends anything to the original author's servers: telemetry, log upload and the install-counting mirror are removed.

Based on Jellyscribe 2.10.0. New: shows you watch are now marked as Currently watching on Serializd the first time an episode is logged, so they appear on your Serializd profile instead of only in the diary. Shows you have already finished in Jellyfin are left alone. Also includes the two fixes from 2.10.0.1: history survives renaming a Jellyfin user, and later anime seasons that Serializd lists as one long season are logged at their running episode number.

Based on Jellyscribe 2.10.0, plus two fixes that are not in the official release yet. Renaming a Jellyfin user no longer empties their history or weakens the duplicate checks, because history is now tied to the Jellyfin user rather than their name. Later seasons of anime that Serializd lists as one long season, such as The Apothecary Diaries season 2, are logged to Serializd at their running episode number instead of being skipped.
